_about: The wind out in the countryside, per weather look (Game.wind_strength, read from today's weather in the morning). strength 0 (dead calm) .. 1 (a gale): the grass tufts (GrassTufts) and the bamboo sway (OutdoorProps.Sway) take it through FarmWorld.set_wind. At 0 they sway as they always did. Above 0 the tips swing further (about 1 + 1.5 x strength times the sway), the wave runs faster (the bamboo about 1 + 0.6 x strength, the grass's time about 1 + 0.56 x strength) and comes in gusts (a slow swell on the amplitude, 0.8 x strength either way, and a quicker flutter). The same Sway moves the kadomatsu's pine, the fence's leafy shoots (leaves, still at 0) and the noren, stall curtains and race banner (cloth, by the square root of the strength, still at 0); its numbers are in OutdoorProps.Sway. The look decides it (a winter storm is a blizzard). There is no cloudy weather in data/weather.json, so the calm sunny days hold the low end; rain is medium, snow a light wind, storm and blizzard strong. Balance numbers are ours.

flat._about: Flat-view only: the tall crops' sway (CropPatches.sway_tip, the 3D shader's own swing in pixels). `rate`: sway frames a second (the view redraws that often while the wind blows and tall crops stand, not every frame). `bands`: how many strips a plant picture is cut into, each shifted sideways by whole pixels (the shader's height weight (1 - v)^2 at the strip's middle), so the top strips lean the most and the root row never moves. A sunny breeze swings the tip under a pixel (a 1 px twitch at a gust's crest), rain gives 1 px, a gusty storm 2 px.
flat._glint_about: The water patches' glint in the flat view (CropPatches.glint_dots): one or two pale pixels on each winter patch's top row, drifting sideways by whole pixels. `rate`: glint frames a second (slower than the sway; the view redraws only when the frame changes). `speed`: the drift's phase in radians a second in still air (0.9 is a slow wander, about a 7 s cycle). `faster`: how much the wind adds to that speed (1 means a gale doubles it, so rain and storm run quicker than a sunny day). `swing`: the drift's reach, in pixels from the middle of the patch. Nothing is drawn while snow lies on the ground. Balance numbers are ours.

3d._about: The 3D view's winter water patches' glint (CropClusters.WATER_SHADER, the same drift as the flat view's, worked out on the GPU from the instance's place): one or two pale texels on the second row of the patch picture (the colour is data/paddy.json water.shine), drifting sideways by whole texels. `rate`, `speed`, `faster` and `swing` mean what they do in "flat".glint (frames a second, phase speed in radians a second, how much the wind adds, texels from the middle). The shader reads the wind as the rice does; none while snow lies on the ground (cover > 0). Balance numbers are ours.

part._about: Grass tufts and tall crops (rice, corn) parting round the farmer's feet and the villagers' and the dog's in the 3D view (Parting, fed each frame by FarmWorld.set_farmer). `max` 8: the most pushers at once, the farmer first and then the ones nearest them (the shader's array holds 8; a village lane has a few figures, so the cap is rarely met and the ones past it are far from the view's centre anyway); the pushes add but never bend a tip further than `bend`, so two figures side by side look like one. A plant whose root is within `radius` cells of a pusher's feet has its tip pushed straight away from them, `bend` cells within `full` x `radius` of the feet, easing to nothing at the radius by a smoothstep, and lowered by `dip` times the push (a bent blade is shorter). It is by distance alone, so the plants spring back as the farmer walks on. radius 1.0: about one cell round the farmer, so the plants in the cells beside them bend and the next ones over stand. full 0.3: the plants the farmer's sprite hides (within about a third of a cell) are not the ones that show the parting, so the full bend reaches out to them and the ease-out falls on the plants just beside the feet, where it can be seen. Grass 0.18: a tuft is 0.15..0.3 high, so its tip lies over about as far as it is tall at the feet and half that beside them (0.12 moved a tuft beside the feet under a pixel at the game's 480 x 270); crops 0.22: a rice hill or a corn stalk is about 0.8..1.2 high, so it leans by about a fifth, enough to read past the farmer's sprite without the clusters looking flattened. dip 0.45: the tip comes down a little as it leans. Balance numbers are ours.
